about: What each state lets car insurers use to set a price. Every entry quotes the law it comes from. A factor that isn't listed for a state hasn't been reviewed yet; it is never read as allowed.

credit.summary: Insurers can use your credit only alongside other factors, and must re-rate you on fresh information at least every two years.
credit.quote: An insurer may use a consumer's credit history or insurance score to cancel, deny, nonrenew, underwrite, or rate personal insurance only in combination with other substantive underwriting factors.

moreSources.label: Alaska Stat. § 21.36.460(c)
moreSources.quote: not later than 24 months after the insurer most recently used the consumer's credit history or insurance score to underwrite or rate a policy, the insurer shall reunderwrite and rerate the policy

credit.summary: Insurers can't price you on the kind of card you carry, and, unless the state approves, not on how many credit checks you have or on a missing or thin credit file.
credit.quote: Insurers shall not deny personal insurance coverage, calculate an insurance score, determine personal insurance premiums or rates, or place an applicant in a tier based in whole or in part on the following types of credit history: (a) An applicant’s number of credit inquiries unless said insurer files and the Department concurs with actuarial documentation which supports other practices. (b) The type of credit card, charge card, or debit card used by an applicant.

moreSources.label: Ala. Admin. Code r. 482-1-127-.05(3)
moreSources.quote: If an applicant is eligible for a particular rate or tier, based on all other criteria, except for the fact that an applicant’s credit history is unavailable (“no-hit”) or incomplete (“thin file”) for that applicant, the applicant will be given that rate or tier unless said insurer files and the Department concurs with actuarial documentation which supports other practices.

credit.summary: Insurers can use your credit, but can't count medical debt in collections, bankruptcies more than seven years old, or your total available credit against you.
credit.quote: F. An insurer shall not use the following types of credit history to calculate an insurance score to determine property or casualty premiums for insurance transactions that are subject to this article and shall not knowingly use an insurance score developed by a third party if the score is calculated using any of the following types of credit history: 1. The absence of credit history or the inability to determine the consumer's credit history unless the insurer's action is actuarially justified or the insurer treats the consumer as if the consumer had neutral credit information, as defined by the insurer. 2. Credit history or an insurance score based on collection accounts identified with a medical industry code. 3. A bankruptcy or a lien satisfaction that is more than seven years old.
